candidateAssessment.concept: Mathematical Modelling, Earth Systems and Energy
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strongest feasible trial contains calculus, numerical methods, signals, programming, mechanics and thermodynamics in sustainability, introductory spectroscopy, geophysical surveying, robotics and energy-system design. These are direct and complementary contributions. They do not form a cumulative inquiry into physical laws through mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum and thermal physics with experimental verification.

candidateAssessment.concept: Biomedical Systems, Image Analysis and Modelling
candidateAssessment.assessment: Anatomy and brain and behaviour introduce imaging in biomedical contexts. Digital image analysis, signals, mathematical modelling and life science form a coherent biomedical methods programme. Acquisition physics, instrumentation and sustained biophysical experiments are absent.

Mathematics and computation supply substantive tools. The workbook has introductory physics topics in sustainability and applied work in robotics and geoscience. It does not provide the cumulative fundamental, particle, quantum and experimental studies needed to organise the degree.
Communication and mathematics are transferable. The disciplinary physics and physics-education progression is not supported by the current curriculum.

academicFinding: UCR offers mathematics, computation and applied study of energy and environmental systems. It includes some mechanics, thermodynamics, waves and spectroscopy. Even combined in a feasible programme, these courses do not provide sustained study of mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and experimental physics. Those subjects underpin Groningen’s advanced courses and research project.
